title: Electricity
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Electricity Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Standard circuit symbols; electrical charge and current (Q = It); current, resistance and potential difference (V = IR); resistors and I–V characteristics of a resistor, filament lamp and diode; thermistors and LDRs; series and parallel circuits; direct and alternating potential difference; mains electricity; power (P = IV, P = I²R); energy transfers in everyday appliances (E = Pt, E = QV); the National Grid.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on electricity: charge and current, V = IR, series and parallel circuits, I–V graphs, thermistors and LDRs, power, mains electricity and the National Grid. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: V = IR, Q = It, P = IV
key_sub: Series: resistances add. Parallel: total resistance is less than the smallest.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current is the rate of flow of charge.

  • Q = It, V = IR, P = IV = I²R, E = Pt = QV.
  • Series: same current everywhere, p.d. shared, resistances add. Parallel: same p.d. across each branch, currents add.
  • UK mains: 230 V a.c. at 50 Hz. Live (brown), neutral (blue), earth (green and yellow).
Example

2 A for 30 s. Charge?

Q = 2 × 30

Answer: 60 C

Example

3 A through 4 Ω. Power?

P = I²R = 9 × 4

Answer: 36 W

Common mistakes

  • Thinking current is used up in a circuit.
  • Thinking the earth wire normally carries current.
  • Using P = I × R instead of P = I²R.

faq.q: What are the main electricity equations at GCSE?
faq.a: Q = It, V = IR, P = IV, P = I²R, E = Pt and E = QV.

faq.q: What do the three wires in a plug do?
faq.a: The live wire (brown) carries the supply p.d., the neutral wire (blue) completes the circuit, and the earth wire (green and yellow) is a safety wire.

faq.q: How do thermistors and LDRs behave?
faq.a: A thermistor's resistance falls as temperature rises. An LDR's resistance falls as light gets brighter.
